evals.prompt: We're Verrata, a payroll-compliance SaaS, 110 people, selling into HR ops. Six weeks ago we signed a technology partnership with Skiplane, an HRIS platform. I need a joint GTM plan I can put in front of our leadership offsite on the 9th. Where things stand: my counterpart there is a marketing manager called Dana. I've emailed her VP twice asking for an intro and got nothing back. Dana was enthusiastic at first but it's been three weeks since her last reply. We both sell into HR ops so honestly the better-together angle writes itself, two logos and one audience. We've got $12k set aside; I have no idea what Skiplane has. Give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to produce a signable plan, with the readiness gate failures named individually and the specific missing pieces listed as the precondition for restarting.
expectations: Declines to produce a finished joint GTM plan and states that the readiness gate failed before any planning happens
Names the absence of an executive sponsor on the Skiplane side as a disqualifier
Names the partner's three weeks of silence, or unresponsiveness generally, as a disqualifier
Names the unknown partner-side budget or capacity as a disqualifier
Rejects "we both sell into HR ops, two logos and one audience" as a joint value proposition and states it fails the neither-alone test
States that a plan cannot fix an unstaffed partnership, rather than proposing a workaround that proceeds anyway
Requires a named owner and a named executive sponsor on each side, four names in total, before planning resumes
Does not invent a launch date, a campaign format, or a budget split for Skiplane
Does not treat Verrata's $12k as sufficient to proceed on one-sided funding

evals.prompt: Kelvinbase (data observability, 60 people) and Margrove, a BI vendor, both sell to analytics teams. We shipped a two-way connector in July. My CMO wants sourced pipeline from this partnership landing inside the quarter, and the quarter closes in seven weeks. I'm the only person on partner marketing and I can give this maybe six hours a week; our designer is booked solid until December. Margrove's team is about the same size as ours. My shortlist right now is a co-authored benchmark report built from both products' telemetry, or a shared booth at the big analytics conference in February. Which one, and what's the plan?
evals.expected_output: Both shortlisted formats deleted for stated reasons, a re-ranked shortlist of remaining formats with trade-offs, and an explicit recommendation naming which constraint moved which format.
expectations: Deletes the co-authored benchmark report and states the reason, a quarter-long format against a seven-week results date and a six-hour weekly ceiling
Deletes the February conference booth and states the reason, the fixed date falls outside the window results must land in
Removes the ruled-out formats from the menu rather than ranking them last or holding them as fallbacks
Presents two or three remaining candidate formats with trade-offs instead of a single option
Identifies the joint webinar as the highest-efficiency B2B format, value bought per unit of two-company coordination, rather than choosing by cost or by audience size
Says explicitly which answer moved which format, for example that the seven-week results date deleted the quarter-long formats
Frames effort as coordination across two organizations, whose sign-off chain the format walks, not as money
Distinguishes the launch date from the date results must land
Recommends a format carrying a form or registration because the objective is pipeline
Makes an explicit recommendation and waits for the user's decision instead of drafting the full plan around one format unasked

evals.prompt: Second time around with the same partner. We're Ashgrove, API security, 200 people; the partner is Tillmark, an API gateway vendor. We ran a webinar together last spring, 380 registrants, both sides came out happy, the relationship is solid. Now my VP wants something out of this partnership that's still producing leads eighteen months from now, not another one-hour spike. No fixed date, she said take the time it takes. The thing that's unusual: Ashgrove has three years of anonymized attack-traffic telemetry, Tillmark has gateway-config data from 4,000 deployments, and neither of us can publish anything meaningful from our own half. Budget is already approved on both sides and we have in-house design. What should we run?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation of the co-authored research report, explicitly justified as the format the efficiency ordering normally starves, with the promoting conditions named.
expectations: Recommends the co-authored research report as the campaign shape
States that the co-authored research report is the format the efficiency ordering normally starves, high value and high effort, losing every ratio round
Names the conditions promoting it here: both sides hold data neither can publish alone, the relationship has already survived one campaign, and the deadline is a quarter out or later
States that the compounding-asset mandate, not cost, is what moved the report above the webinar
Notes that in-house design capacity and pre-approved budget remove most of the report's effort penalty
Does not recommend repeating the joint webinar as the primary shape on the grounds that it worked last time
States that the report passes the neither-alone test because the claim requires both data sets
Treats the report as a gated format and therefore triggers the lead-sharing agreement in full
Plans a quarter-scale timeline covering two review chains plus design
Sets the debrief as a calendar date fixed before launch

evals.prompt:
Here's the joint plan my counterpart at Ombrelle sent over. I think it reads well, just a bit flabby. Can you tighten the wording and make it sound sharper for both exec teams?

JOINT MARKETING PLAN - Halvard + Ombrelle
Goal: grow awareness for both brands and generate leads together
Value prop: "Halvard and Ombrelle - better together"
Audience: both companies' audiences
Campaign: co-branded ebook, some social, maybe a webinar
Split: both teams collaborate on the content
Budget: shared marketing budget, TBD
Timeline: launch in Q2
Leads: leads will be shared between the teams
Owners: Halvard growth team + Ombrelle marketing team
Success: engagement, reach, pipeline impact
evals.expected_output: A refusal to rewrite the prose, with each line scored against the pass checklist and the specific decision missing behind it named.
expectations: Declines to polish the wording and states that the missing content is missing decisions, not missing prose
Flags the single merged goal and requires each side's criterion stated separately, each with a number and a date
Flags "Halvard and Ombrelle - better together" as failing the neither-alone test because either name could be swapped for any vendor
Flags "both companies' audiences" as lacking a segment, overlap evidence, and explicit exclusions
Flags "maybe a webinar" as no chosen campaign shape, and requires the rejected alternatives with the reason each was rejected
Flags "both teams collaborate on the content" as naming no creator and no approver per asset
Flags "shared marketing budget, TBD" as carrying no per-side spend line
Flags "launch in Q2" as not a date, and requires one agreed launch date with the approval buffer visible in the phase dates
Flags the leads line as lacking consent basis, transfer mechanism, transfer timing, and a deduplication rule
Flags the owners line as team names rather than four named people, an owner and an executive sponsor on each side
Flags "engagement, reach, pipeline impact" as unmeasurable without per-party tracking links and a sourced-versus-influenced rule, and notes that no debrief date is scheduled

evals.prompt: We're co-hosting a webinar in six weeks: us, Norlens, a contract-lifecycle SaaS headquartered in Dublin, with Pellamont, an e-signature vendor out of Denver. Registrations will come off both sides' lists plus some paid promo, and the audience is legal-ops people across the EU and the US. Pellamont's marketing ops wants to host the form in their instance and push everything into our CRM the week after the event. Their head of demand gen said we'll just put one checkbox saying you agree to hear from both of us. I need the lead-sharing and attribution piece nailed down. Write it.
evals.expected_output: A lead-sharing and attribution section specifying consent parameters, joint-controller split, testable transfer timing, dedup rule, per-party links and the sourced/influenced rule, stopping short of drafted form copy.
expectations: Rejects the single bundled checkbox and requires each company's consent to be separable
Requires the form to name both companies and state the purpose of each company's processing
Requires a withdrawal route as easy as giving consent
Names the legal basis for the transfer explicitly rather than leaving it implied
Identifies the co-hosted webinar registration as a joint-controller situation and requires the responsibility split to be documented and disclosed
States that a lead can exercise rights against either company regardless of the internal split
Treats who owns the form as the control point and assigns the data-subject-request duty to a named side
Replaces "the week after the event" with a testable transfer timing expressed in business days from capture
Requires a qualified-lead definition agreed jointly for this initiative, noting no cross-company standard exists
Requires a deduplication and existing-relationship rule chosen from excluded from transfer, transferred but flagged, or counted for attribution only
Requires per-party tracked links with a shared campaign identifier and source parameters split per company, ruling out a single untagged shared link
Defines sourced and influenced separately for this initiative and states they are reported separately and never merged
Decides the lead-ownership pattern explicitly, either each side keeps its own channels' leads or all shared-asset leads go to both, rather than leaving it open
Delivers consent parameters and mechanics rather than drafted form copy, and states that writing the literal form wording is downstream asset work

evals.prompt: Building the business case for our first co-marketing push with Quorrin. We're Basalt Metrics. Two things I want reflected in the plan's targets. First, I keep seeing that 60-70% of alliances fail, and my CFO wants to know why ours won't. Second, a partnerships-platform report I read says partner-sourced deals close 46% faster and carry 2.3x the deal size, and I want our plan to target that. Also, can you throw in whatever the industry-standard conversion rate is for joint webinars so we've got something to benchmark against?
evals.expected_output: Each quoted figure handled by provenance: the failure rate refused as folklore with its real spread, the vendor figures flagged and refused as targets, the non-existent standard named as such, and the user's own history proposed as baseline.
expectations: Refuses to present "60-70% of alliances fail" as settled fact and identifies it as untraceable folklore
States that published alliance-failure estimates span roughly 20-80% depending on how failure is defined, and presents that spread rather than one number
Flags the 46%-faster and 2.3x-deal-size figures as vendor-self-reported wherever they appear
Explains why such figures are directional marketing claims: self-selected samples, unaudited methodology, incentives pointing one way
Refuses to set a vendor-reported figure as the target the plan must hit
Proposes Basalt Metrics' own historical campaign performance as the baseline instead
States that no industry-standard joint-webinar conversion rate exists to benchmark against
Does not fabricate a specific conversion-rate figure to satisfy the request
Requires every benchmark quoted anywhere in the plan to carry a provenance flag

evals.prompt: Our partner Gravenhorst runs their user conference on 14 October. We're Solvex, 90 people, and we want to launch a joint integration campaign timed to it. Today is 11 September. Internally we'd normally turn a campaign like this around in about four weeks end to end: content, page, emails, promo. Both sides have a small budget and an owner assigned. Give me the sequencing, what happens when, so we hit the 14th.
evals.expected_output: A backwards-anchored six-phase schedule built on a doubled timeline, with the arithmetic shortfall stated and resolved by cutting scope rather than the buffer.
expectations: States that the plan needs roughly double a single-company timeline, about eight weeks against Solvex's four-week solo estimate
Identifies the surplus as the other organization's approval, legal and brand cycles, and calls it structural to two-company work rather than a contingency
States that the roughly five weeks between 11 September and 14 October does not fit the doubled estimate
Cuts scope rather than the approval buffer to make the date fit
Anchors backwards from 14 October: launch first, then the approval gate, then asset deadlines, then signing
Lays out the six phases in order: agree terms, build assets, pre-launch, launch, follow-up, debrief
States that nothing downstream starts until the plan is signed by four named people
Schedules an explicit feedback buffer between each draft deadline and its review deadline
Commits both sides to publishing simultaneously on one agreed date, and states that a staggered launch reads as one company promoting another
Agrees a scope-cut plan upfront naming which asset drops first if the timeline compresses
Sets the debrief as a calendar date before launch and includes a mid-flight check-in between the two owners at a set date

evals.prompt: Quick one. Us, Perlyn, and our partner Astrolume are doing a joint webinar plus a gated checklist. Astrolume writes both pieces, we design them, and we're buying the LinkedIn promo. My counterpart keeps calling this 50/50 and I think that's fine? Separately, Astrolume mentioned they have about $6k of co-op money from a cloud marketplace they could throw at promotion. Their partner marketer said just spend it and we'll sort the paperwork later. How do I write the budget section?
evals.expected_output: A budget section separating money from labor, picking a funding pattern from the ranked three with a recommendation, and recording the co-op fund's terms verbatim with proof, deadline and a named claim owner.
expectations: Separates money from labor and states that "Astrolume writes, Perlyn designs" is a task split, not a budget split
Warns that conflating the two breeds resentment when one side's tasks cost more
Presents the three budget patterns in efficiency order: each side funds its own channels, equal cash lines, then proportional to each side's expected lead share
Recommends one pattern explicitly rather than accepting "50/50" as given
Notes that the proportional pattern is the fairest and loses every ratio round, and names when to promote it anyway
Records each side's spend as its own separate budget line
Rejects "just spend it and we'll sort the paperwork later" for the co-op money
Requires the fund's eligible activities recorded verbatim from the program's terms, including whether an activity plan needs pre-approval before spend
Requires the proof of execution the claim demands and the claim deadline relative to the activity date, both recorded in the plan
Names a specific person on a specific side as owner of filing the claim, and states that an unowned claim goes unclaimed

evals.prompt: Consumer side this time. We're Halona, a DTC electrolyte drink brand, around $14M revenue. We want to do something with Fernpost, an outdoor apparel brand with a much bigger Instagram following, aimed at trail runners. Two ideas on the table: a co-branded limited-edition bottle sold through both our stores, or a content series with a trail-running creator both brands already work with. No fixed deadline. We own our DTC store and a warehouse; Fernpost has retail placement. What do we run and how do I plan it?
evals.expected_output: A consumer-side format decision using the B2C ordering and brand-fit screen, with disclosure and exclusivity handled as consumer-specific, KPIs swapped off pipeline, and the planning spine kept intact.
expectations: Uses the consumer-side format ordering with the creator collaboration as the default, not the B2B ordering
States that the co-branded product is the consumer format the efficiency ordering starves, highest value and losing every ratio round

Names the conditions that would promote the co-branded product anyway: a prior successful collab with this partner, secured retail distribution, and an objective needing a durable artifact rather than a reach spike
Notes that Halona's own store and warehouse plus Fernpost's retail placement remove much of the co-branded product's effort penalty
Puts brand-fit screening first on the grounds that the association itself is the risk
States that sponsored-content disclosure is enforced by consumer regulators and puts the disclosure obligation in the creator agreement
Notes that a missing disclosure is public and unfixable after publication
Treats category exclusivity as an explicitly negotiated contract tier rather than assuming it
Warns that brand veto rights can extend past production into published content, unlike the front-loaded B2B approval chain
Replaces pipeline KPIs with reach, engagement, sell-through or brand lift, and states that attribution here is structurally softer
Keeps the planning spine unchanged: per-side goals with numbers, a signed agreement before asset work, one agreed launch date, named owners on both sides, and a scheduled debrief

evals.prompt: We did a joint webinar with Cadmere back in May. 412 registrations, attendance was decent. Three months on, our sales team says they got nothing usable out of it, Cadmere's partner lead is telling their exec team the webinar sourced most of their Q3 pipeline, and neither of us can prove anything because we just used one shared short link across both sides' promo. Their head of marketing wants to run it again in November. I want to say yes but do it properly. What should the debrief have covered, and what changes for round two?
evals.expected_output: A statement that the attribution split is unrecoverable, the full debrief agenda that was skipped, and the specific mechanics that must predate results in round two.
expectations: States that the sourced-versus-influenced split is unrecoverable after the fact because a single untagged shared link was used, and does not attempt to reconstruct it
Requires per-party tracked links from day one in round two, with a shared campaign identifier and source parameters split per company
Traces the attribution dispute to the absence of a lead-ownership rule agreed before the results existed

Lays out the debrief agenda covering results against each side's own goal side by side, lead quality against the agreed definition, collaboration quality, the neither-alone retrospective, and a recorded decision
Includes the case where one side hit and the other missed as an explicit debrief output
Requires a recorded decision of repeat, reshape or stop, and states that an undecided debrief schedules a decision date
States that "nothing usable" and "sourced most of Q3 pipeline" are not comparable without a jointly agreed qualified-lead definition
Requires the round-two debrief date to be booked at the agree-terms phase, before launch
Sets one attribution window used identically by both sides, and has each side compute its own return on its own spend rather than one blended number

evals.prompt: New VP joined and wants us nearbound and ecosystem-led by Q1. Concretely he's asked me for three things: build the joint GTM plan with Vantiq Systems using the standard joint business plan template; set our Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 launch criteria so we know how much marketing muscle each partner launch gets; and run account mapping first, since that's the discipline everything else depends on. We're Karst Data, 140 people. Give me all three.
evals.expected_output: The vendor-coined vocabulary graded as such, the non-existent template and tier standards named plainly, and the plan built section by section with the user deciding the program-specific parameters.
expectations: Identifies "nearbound" and "ecosystem-led growth" as vocabulary originating with one vendor and its acquired media brands, not as established doctrine
Treats that vocabulary as usable shared language while refusing to build the plan's logic on it
Notes that account mapping as a named discipline was popularized by the same vendor
States plainly that no canonical joint business plan or joint GTM plan template exists
Presents the plan skeleton as assembled practice to validate section by section rather than as an industry-standard form
States that Tier 1/2/3 launch criteria are program-specific with no standard, and makes Karst Data decide them explicitly
Does not invent published thresholds for the launch tiers
Notes that frameworks borrowed from outside partner marketing, such as RACI, OKRs or phase-gate, are real but not partner-marketing inventions and should not be force-fit
Presents each section for validation before drafting the next rather than delivering all three artifacts at once
